title: add-entropy-guided-invocation-sampler-and-session-flamegraph-summaries
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Long conversational sessions and evolving prompt shapes have produced low-frequency but high-impact cost/latency tail events that escape uniform sampling and cause noisy SLO alerts. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: 1) an entropy-guided invocation sampler that biases trace sampling toward invocations with high token-level entropy, abrupt token-cost drift, or rare argument shapes; and 2) a session flamegraph summarizer that compacts long multi-turn invocations into stage-level frames (prompt, model-run, tool-calls, post-processing) with stacked token-cost/latency bars so humans can quickly scan where cost accumulates across a session. The description below lists changes, tests, reviewers' discussion, CI results, and deployment notes.

What this does (high level):
- Add entropy-based scoring to the invocation sampler (telemetry/sampler/*). Sampler computes a lightweight per-invocation entropy estimate and a delta token-cost drift metric; these are combined into a dynamic sampling weight so we retain more traces from noisy long-tail cases without increasing overall storage significantly.
- Add a session flamegraph summarizer (observability/flamegraph/*) that reduces long token streams into a compact JSON summary and a small set of representative spans for trace UI and alert links.
- Dashboard: new "Session Flamegraph" panel and a "Entropy Drift Explorer" heatmap in observability/dashboards/session-flamegraph.json.
- Alert tuning: new rule that warns only when entropy-weighted cost percentiles exceed baseline AND the session flamegraph indicates concentrated cost in the model-run stage (reduces false positives from client-side retries).
- Tests: unit tests for sampler heuristics, e2e replay bench to validate sampling budget, and a small perf microbench for summarizer latency.

Why this is different: existing sampling is mostly frequency- or cost-proportional which misses high-entropy failure modes (e.g., malformed prompts, adversarial inputs, or sudden prompt-shape drift). Entropy-guided sampling targets those rare but high-value traces. The session flamegraph focuses investigator attention on stage-level attribution rather than token-level noise so SREs and engineers can triage faster.

review_comments: Ben Rosen: The entropy score looks promising — can you add a short note on calibration knobs so operators can tune aggressiveness?
Priya Nair: Added `sampling.alpha` and `sampling.min_rate` config with sensible defaults (0.6, 0.01). Updated docs. Will also expose via Console feature flag.
Elena Kovacs: Summarizer CPU cost needs a bound for 99th pct sessions — suggest a max-token window and an async fallback to write a 'light' summary if cost hits the cap.
Priya Nair: Implemented async fallback and max_window=8192 tokens. Documented the behavior and added perf test covering pathological sessions.
Samir Gupta: Alert rule looks good. Confirmed reduced noise in replaybench — overall alert volume dropped ~34% in synthetic runs.
Ben Rosen: Approve after CI green.
release_notes: Add entropy-weighted sampling and session flamegraph summaries to improve signal quality for SLO alerts and accelerate long-session triage. Config knobs: sampling.alpha, sampling.min_rate, summarizer.max_window.
deployment_notes: Feature gated behind Console flag (obs.entropy_sampler). Rolling deploy: sampler hot reconfigurable, summarizer runs as sidecar on observability workers. No DB migrations. Monitor `obs.sampler.sample_rate` and `obs.flamegraph.latency_p99` during rollout.
